HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.summary: Neither library contains any Shimura theory: grep of both trees finds no Shimura datum, Shimura variety, Hilbert modular variety, Hilbert-Blumenthal abelian scheme, polarization of an abelian scheme, dual abelian variety, Weil pairing on an abelian scheme, p-divisible group, Hasse invariant, Deligne-Pappas or Rapoport locus, and no Weil restriction of group schemes. What exists is substrate: Mathlib's totally real number fields, Dirichlet unit theorem and regulator, quaternion algebras, upper half-plane, congruence subgroups and classical SL2(Z) modular forms; TauCeti's abelian varieties over a field (proper geometrically integral group schemes, with End/Hom and isogenies but no dual and no polarization), its affine algebraic-group library (centre, derived subgroup, GL_n, symplectic groups, tori), its pure Hodge structures with polarizations, its narrow class group and totally positive elements, and its central simple algebra / Brauer-group development for quaternion algebras. Genuinely missing is essentially everything the roadmap states: the two Hilbert data and their domains, abelian schemes with real multiplication and c-polarizations, the moduli problems and their representability, integral models at ramified p, the ordinary locus and Hasse ideal, unit actions on polarization classes, p-level structures, Shimura curves for quaternion algebras, definite quaternionic algebraic modular forms, etale/Betti cohomology with Hecke correspondences, and Cerednik-Drinfeld uniformisation. Note that ShimuraData D5 and PELModuli M5 already claim the Hilbert data and the trace-pairing PEL datum, so H0-H1 substantially duplicate layers of the prerequisite roadmaps.

targets.target: The group G = Res_{F/Q} GL_2 (Weil restriction of scalars of a linear algebraic group)
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'weil restriction|restriction of scalars' over both trees returns only module/algebra restriction of scalars (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/RestrictScalars.lean and friends); there is no Weil restriction of schemes or of group schemes anywhere. TauCeti has an affine algebraic-group library (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/) with GL_n, SL_n, tori and symplectic groups, but no restriction-of-scalars functor.

targets.target: The subgroup G* = G x_{Res Gm} Gm cut out by scalar determinant
targets.note: Depends on the previous target; no fibre product of algebraic groups along determinant and scalar inclusion is constructed. TauCeti has determinant as a character of GL_n (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Determinant.lean) but no such fibre product.

What is missing is the group G at all, hence any description of its centre Res_{F/Q} Gm or of the common derived group of G and G*.

targets.target: The datum morphism G* -> G is the expected inclusion; both reflex fields are Q

targets.note: The trace form, the inverse different and the symplectic group all exist separately, and TauCeti has symplectic algebraic groups (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Symplectic/), but the trace-pairing symplectic representation of G* is not constructed because G* is not constructed.

MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.summary: Nothing of the metaplectic theory itself is in either library: grep -rn -i over both whole trees finds no occurrence of 'Heisenberg', 'Stone-von Neumann', 'metaplectic', 'Weil index', 'Weil representation', 'oscillator', 'Schwartz-Bruhat', 'dual pair', 'theta kernel', 'Jacobi form', 'Whittaker' or 'half-integral weight', and there is no Hilbert symbol in either library. What is present is the analytic and algebraic substrate: Mathlib's Haar measure on locally compact groups, Pontryagin dual, Fourier transform on a vector space over a local field with inversion, Schwartz space, Gaussian Fourier transforms, Poisson summation for Schwartz functions on Z subset R, the restricted product construction, adele rings and idele groups of a number field, abstract group extensions, quadratic forms with discriminants and Gauss sums, together with TauCeti's symplectic forms, symplectic algebraic groups, group extensions with factor sets and their H^2 classification, and Hermite/Fourier L^2 analysis. Classically, Mathlib has the one- and two-variable Jacobi theta functions with their S- and T-transformation laws — the g = 1 shadow of MP.5's theta kernel. Genuinely missing is the whole roadmap: the Heisenberg group of a symplectic space, Stone-von Neumann, the metaplectic cover and Weil cocycle, the Weil index and its Hilbert-symbol identities, dual pairs and theta modules, the adelic cover with its canonical splitting, adelic theta kernels and genuine automorphic spaces, half-integral weight forms, Jacobi forms and the genus-two cover.

targets.target: Finite-dimensional symplectic space W over a local field and its automorphisms
targets.note: TauCeti bundles a nondegenerate alternating form as SymplecticForm (over a real/complex module, in the almost-complex-structure file) and has symplectic algebraic groups over a ring; Mathlib has the symplectic matrix group with det = 1 and alternating bilinear forms. None of these is set up over a general local field with its topology, which is what MP.0 needs.

targets.target: The Heisenberg central extension of W with group law given by half the alternating pairing, its inverse and symplectic automorphisms
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'heisenberg' over both trees returns nothing. TauCeti has abstract group extensions with factor sets, but no Heisenberg group is constructed.

targets.target: Polarizations of W, their change maps, local compactness and Haar normalization
targets.note: Haar measure with existence and uniqueness up to scalar is fully available in Mathlib for locally compact groups, but there are no Lagrangian polarizations of a symplectic space and no self-dual normalization attached to an additive character.

targets.target: Schrodinger models on Schwartz-Bruhat functions; Hilbert and smooth-vector realizations at infinity
targets.note: Mathlib's Schwartz space is defined on a normed vector space (the archimedean case only); there is no Schwartz-Bruhat space over a nonarchimedean local field or over the adeles (grep -rn -i 'schwartz.?bruhat' returns nothing), and no induced representation model of the Heisenberg group.

targets.target: Central character and translation/modulation relations with the chosen Fourier convention
targets.note: Mathlib has the Fourier transform against a general additive character of a commutative group acting on a vector space, its translation/modulation identities and Fourier inversion, plus the Pontryagin dual; what is missing is the Heisenberg representation these would be the relations of.

duplicates.note: AL.0 owns local Schwartz-Bruhat spaces, Fourier transforms, self-duality of local additive groups and the restricted tensor-product adelic space — the same substrate MP.0 builds its Schrodinger models on.

targets.target: Stone-von Neumann: uniqueness of the irreducible Heisenberg representation with a fixed nontrivial central character
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'stone.?von.?neumann' over both trees returns nothing; there is no Heisenberg group and no such uniqueness theorem in any category.

targets.target: Intertwining operators for symplectic transformations and their scalar ambiguity
targets.note: No intertwiner theory for these representations exists; Mathlib's Schur-lemma material is about modules over a ring, not unitary representations of a locally compact group.

targets.target: The topological central extension built from the intertwiners; identification of the double cover by the normalized Weil-index cocycle
targets.note: Mathlib has abstract group extensions with sections and splittings, and TauCeti classifies extensions by factor sets and their H^2 class, including the central case; but these are extensions of abstract groups — there is no topological/continuous central extension theory, and no Weil cocycle.

targets.target: Associativity, continuity, coboundary-independence, and comparison of the scalar extension with the double-cover model
targets.note: The coboundary-independence part is abstractly available from TauCeti's H^2 classification, but continuity and the specific comparison of the C^1-extension with the two-fold cover are not stated anywhere.

targets.target: Genuine representations with central -1 acting by -1
targets.note: No genuine representations of a cover group exist in either library.

targets.target: The Weil index of a nondegenerate quadratic form via a normalized oscillatory/Fourier integral
targets.note: Mathlib computes the Fourier transform of a Gaussian over R and has classical Gauss sums over finite fields (with the quadratic Gauss sum), which are the archimedean and residual shadows of the Weil index; the Weil index itself is defined nowhere (grep -rn -i 'weil index' returns nothing).

targets.target: Orthogonal-sum, scaling, discriminant and Hilbert-symbol identities for the Weil index, including dyadic factors
targets.note: The discriminant of a quadratic form exists in Mathlib, but there is no Hilbert symbol in either library (grep -rn -i 'hilbert symbol' over both trees returns nothing), so none of these identities can even be stated.

targets.target: The Weil representation on unipotent, Levi and Fourier generators, with their relations, agreeing with the intrinsic representation of MP.1
targets.note: No Weil representation in either library.

targets.target: Change-of-additive-character and dual/conjugate formulas
targets.note: Mathlib's Fourier transform is stated for a general additive character, so change-of-character is available at the level of the transform, but not for the Weil index or the Weil representation.

targets.target: Orthogonal-symplectic and unitary dual-pair embeddings and the restriction of the metaplectic cover to them
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'dual pair' over both trees finds only unrelated hits; no reductive dual pairs exist.

targets.target: Splitting statements with auxiliary characters, dimensions and parity
targets.note: Nothing to split: the cover does not exist.

targets.target: Big theta modules as coinvariants and small theta quotients
targets.note: No smooth representation theory of p-adic groups exists in either library (no admissible/smooth representation class, no Jacquet functor).

targets.target: Equivariance, admissibility/finite-length, see-saw identities, Jacquet filtrations and first-occurrence/vanishing comparisons
targets.note: None of these notions are present; the only representation theory in the libraries is of finite groups, Lie algebras and algebraic groups.

targets.note: Mathlib has a general restricted-product construction with its topology, and the adele ring and idele group of a number field built from it; but there are no adelic points of an algebraic group, and no local covers to take the restricted product of.

targets.target: Product formula for Weil indices and the canonical splitting over the rational symplectic group
targets.note: No Weil index, hence no product formula. Mathlib does have the product formula for absolute values of a number field, which is a different statement.

targets.note: There is no restricted tensor product of representations and no adelic Schwartz-Bruhat space in either library.

targets.target: Compatibility with the rational splitting, local choices and changes of additive character; explicit treatment of the finite central quotient

targets.note: Mathlib has the classical one- and two-variable Jacobi theta functions, i.e. the theta series of the rank-one lattice Z with the standard Gaussian, but no theta series attached to a general quadratic space and no Weil-representation transform in the summand.

OverconvergentAutomorphicForms.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. grep -rn -i over both whole trees finds no 'overconvergent', no 'Igusa', no 'Hida', no 'locally analytic' representation or distribution theory, no rigid-analytic weight space, no 'anticanonical' locus, no automorphy cocycle in the p-adic setting, and no Koecher principle; and since the roadmap's geometric base (the Hilbert integral models and towers of H2-H4, and the Hodge-Tate period maps of T3-T5) is itself absent from the libraries, there is nothing to put a coefficient sheaf on. The substrate that does exist is real: Mathlib's p-adic numbers and integers with the Mahler basis and the Amice transform, abstract measures (the Iwasawa-algebra construction), continuous monoid homomorphisms, ultrametric normed spaces and compact operators, Grothendieck topologies with sheaves and the sheaf condition as an equalizer, torsors (algebraic and topological), filtered colimits; and TauCeti's adic-space development (valuation spectra, Huber pairs, Spa with rational subsets, the structure presheaf and its sheaf criterion, polydiscs), its Fredholm theory with compact perturbations, and its classical modular-forms and Hecke-operator library. Genuinely missing is the entire construction: geometric and arithmetic Hilbert weight spaces, analytic coefficient modules, equivariant sheaves from cocycles, the BHW automorphy factor and its domains, integral lattices, arithmetic descent, the AIP comparison, cusp forms and Hecke/U_p operators with complete continuity, the Igusa/Hida comparison, and the Siegel and unitary instantiations.

PadicFamilies.summary: Almost none of this roadmap is built, but one layer is a genuine exception. L0a's first paragraph — the Fitting decomposition of a finite module under an endomorphism U into its eventually invertible image and eventually killed kernel — is proved in Mathlib in greater generality, for any endomorphism of a module that is both Artinian and Noetherian (LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow and LinearMap.isCompl_iSup_ker_pow_iInf_range_pow, sorry-free), together with the bijectivity statements IsArtinian.surjective_of_injective_endomorphism and IsNoetherian.injective_of_surjective_endomorphism and a full IsIdempotentElem API; what is still missing there is the projector e itself as the stable value of U^(n!), its equivariance and naturality, and the whole profinite inverse-limit and exactness package. Everything else is absent: grep over both trees finds no p-adic modular form, ordinary tower, Igusa tower, Hida theory, ordinary projector, modular symbol, eigenvariety, eigencurve, Fredholm hypersurface, orthonormalizable Banach module, p-adic L-function, pseudorepresentation or Selmer complex. The classical substrate is strong — Mathlib's modular forms with the q-expansion map and its injectivity, Eisenstein series, the abstract Hecke ring, and TauCeti's very large classical Hecke-operator, diamond-operator, newform, multiplicity-one and degeneracy-map development, plus Mathlib's Iwasawa-algebra ingredients (abstract measures, Mahler basis, Amice transform) and compact-operator theory — but nothing p-adic-analytic is built on it.

targets.target: p-adic modular forms from the ordinary tower and their spaces of q-expansions
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'igusa|ordinary locus|overconvergent|hida' over both trees returns nothing; no p-adic modular form of any flavour exists in either library.

targets.target: The q-expansion principle, integral level structures and diamond actions
targets.note: Mathlib proves that a complex modular form for a congruence subgroup is determined by its q-expansion at infinity (hypotheses: 0 < h and h a strict period of the group), and TauCeti builds diamond operators on Gamma_1(N)-forms with their multiplicativity; this is the analytic q-expansion injectivity, not the geometric q-expansion principle over a base ring, and there are no integral level structures because there are no modular curves.

targets.target: Finite generation, finite flatness and control for ordinary cuspidal modules and Hecke algebras over weight Iwasawa algebras
targets.note: The Iwasawa algebra as a space of abstract measures and the classical Hecke algebra of a Hecke triple both exist, and TauCeti has an extensive classical T_n/diamond development; there is no ordinary Hecke algebra, no ordinary projector applied to it, and no control theorem.

targets.target: The ordinary Eisenstein family and the identification of its q-expansion
targets.note: Mathlib has classical Eisenstein series as modular forms (with E_4, E_6 and their q-expansions); there is no p-stabilization, no measure-valued family and no Iwasawa-algebra coefficient.

targets.target: Specialization at arithmetic characters to the correct classical ordinary space with nebentypus, p-stabilization and multiplicity
targets.note: TauCeti has newforms with multiplicity one and strong multiplicity one classically, but there is no family to specialize and no p-stabilization operator.

duplicates.note: L4 there constructs the Eisenstein measure family and its q-expansion (RJW Theorem 8.2) and explicitly defers the overconvergent/Hida realization to this roadmap; the Eisenstein family is stated in both.
R21.2 imports ordinary families, the ordinary Hecke algebra and Hida control from L0 and adds only the nearly ordinary/Eisenstein statements.

targets.target: Fitting decomposition of a finite module under an endomorphism U into eventually invertible image and eventually killed kernel
targets.note: Mathlib proves the Fitting decomposition M = ker(f^n) ⊕ range(f^n) for large n, and M = (sup_n ker f^n) ⊕ (inf_n range f^n), for an endomorphism of a module that is [IsArtinian R M] and [IsNoetherian R M] — strictly more general than L0a's 'finite underlying module', which is both. The file has no sorry. IsArtinian.surjective_of_injective_endomorphism and IsNoetherian.injective_of_surjective_endomorphism give the invertibility of U on the stable image.

targets.target: U^(n!) eventually constant with value the projector e; e² = e, U-equivariance and naturality
targets.note: The decomposition that determines e is there and Mathlib has a full idempotent-element API, but the specific element e = lim U^(n!) is not constructed: grep -n 'factorial' in Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Eigenspace/Zero.lean returns nothing, and no naturality statement for maps commuting with U exists.

targets.target: The profinite projector: e as the inverse limit of finite projectors over M = lim M/J, with pointwise convergence of U^(n!), continuity, image/kernel decomposition, invertibility on eM and topological nilpotence on (1-e)M
targets.note: No such inverse-limit construction exists in either library; grep -rn -i 'ordinary projector' over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Exactness of e for U-equivariant exact sequences of finite modules, then for inverse-limit sequences under Mittag-Leffler/compact-surjectivity hypotheses
targets.note: Mathlib has the Mittag-Leffler condition for cofiltered systems and exactness of filtered/cofiltered limits in the usual settings, but nothing about exactness of an ordinary projector.

targets.target: Degreewise application to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U, and compatibility with cohomology under the chosen limits
targets.note: Mathlib has homological algebra with complexes and cohomology, but no ordinary-part functor on them.

duplicates.note: PA.2 consumes exactly this projector and restates the finite-quotient/continuity hypotheses and the failure test for an arbitrary complete Noetherian ring; the construction is owned here.
R21.1 consumes L0a's ordinary projectors and their finite-level comparison and applies them to Hecke complexes.

QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms.summary: This is the one roadmap in the batch with substantial library coverage, and it is concentrated in the first two layers. Mathlib has partitions (Nat.Partition with odds, distincts and restricted families), the partition generating function as a formal power series together with its infinite-product form and the coefficientwise finiteness that makes the product converge (Nat.Partition.genFun, hasProd_genFun, multipliable_genFun, genFun_eq_tprod), and Glaisher's theorem with Euler's odd = distinct corollary; it also has the Dedekind eta function with nonvanishing, differentiability, logDeriv eta = E2, the S-transformation eta(-1/z) = (sqrt I)^{-1} sqrt z eta(z), the modular discriminant Delta = eta^24 as a genuine level-one cusp form with its T- and S-invariance, and the one- and two-variable Jacobi theta functions with their functional equations (including the half-integral-weight law theta(S.tau) = (-I tau)^{1/2} theta(tau)). All of these files are sorry-free. What is missing is everything analytic and everything beyond level one: no q-binomial/q-Pochhammer identities, no partition congruences, no Jacobi forms with index, no Kloosterman sums, no Bessel functions, no Hardy-Ramanujan/Rademacher asymptotics or exact formula, no Maass forms or weight-k hyperbolic Laplacian, no xi operator, no mock modular forms or Zwegers completions, no quantum modular forms or radial limits, and no moonshine — Mathlib has vertex operators as Hahn-series-valued maps but no vertex algebra, and TauCeti has only a transcribed Y_443 presentation of the Monster, with no j-function anywhere in either library.

targets.target: Partition functions and restricted partition families
targets.note: Partitions of a natural number are a finite type in Mathlib with the odd, distinct and part-restricted subfamilies; the file is sorry-free.

targets.target: Generating products for partition counts, as formal power series
targets.note: Mathlib builds the generating function attached to an arbitrary character f(i, c) of a part and its multiplicity and proves it equals the infinite product prod_i (1 + sum_j f(i,j) X^{ij}) in the X-adic topology; the specializations to restricted and count-restricted partitions are proved in Glaisher.lean. The module docstring records that the specialization giving the unrestricted partition function p(n) itself is still a TODO, so the classical product formula for sum p(n) q^n is not yet a named theorem.

targets.target: Coefficientwise finiteness of infinite products and specialization maps
targets.note: Multipliability of the product in the X-adic (pi) topology on R[[X]] is proved, which is exactly the coefficientwise finiteness the layer asks for; PowerSeries.subst and PowerSeries.rescale give the formal specialization maps.

targets.target: q-binomial identities
targets.note: grep -i for qBinomial, gaussianBinomial, qChoose and qPochhammer over declarations.tsv returns nothing in either library; Mathlib's Pochhammer is the ordinary ascending factorial, not its q-analogue.

targets.target: Partition congruences in formal power-series rings
targets.note: Euler's identity and Glaisher's generalization are proved, but there are no congruences in the Ramanujan sense: grep -rn -i 'partition congru|p(5n' over both trees returns nothing.

duplicates.note: CA.2 owns recurrences, binomial identities and rational/formal generating functions with the same 'prove coefficient identities formally first' acceptance clause; QM.0 restates the formal-generating-function discipline for partitions.

targets.target: Theta functions with their transformation law and branch choice
targets.note: Mathlib proves theta(S.tau) = (-I tau)^(1/2) theta(tau) with the principal branch and theta(T^2.tau) = theta(tau), i.e. the half-integral-weight law at the generators of Gamma_theta, plus the two-variable functional equation; what is missing is the multiplier system on a whole congruence subgroup and the behaviour at every cusp.

targets.target: The Dedekind eta function with its multiplier system
targets.note: eta is defined as q^(1/24) prod (1 - q^(n+1)), proved nonvanishing and differentiable on the upper half-plane, with logDeriv eta = E2 up to the standard constant and the S-transformation eta(-1/z) = (sqrt I)^(-1) sqrt z eta(z); Delta = eta^24 is a level-one cusp form of weight 12 with S- and T-invariance and first q-coefficient 1. Missing is the multiplier system of eta on all of SL_2(Z) (no Dedekind sums exist in either library: grep -rn -i 'dedekind sum' returns nothing) and any eta quotient of higher level.

targets.target: Jacobi forms with multiplier systems, weights and indices
targets.note: The two-variable theta function exists as an analytic function, but there is no definition of a Jacobi form, no index and no elliptic transformation law; grep -rn -i 'jacobi form' over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Cusp behaviour verified at every cusp
targets.note: Mathlib has cusps of a congruence subgroup and the vanishing condition at all of them in the definition of CuspForm, and Delta is shown to vanish at infinity; but for theta and eta only the behaviour at infinity and under the named generators is proved.

duplicates.note: MP.7 owns the half-integral-weight forms and multiplier systems that QM.1 is required to match; the layer names MP.7 as an input and restates the multiplier convention.
MP.8 also defines Jacobi modular forms, theta decomposition and half-integral-weight automorphy factors; the Jacobi-form definition is stated in both layers.

targets.target: The Hardy-Ramanujan asymptotic for p(n)
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'hardy.?ramanujan' over both trees returns nothing; there is no asymptotic for the partition function in either library.

targets.target: Kloosterman sums
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'kloosterman' over both trees returns nothing. Mathlib has Gauss sums over finite fields, which are a different exponential sum, and no Weil bound for Kloosterman sums.

targets.target: Bessel functions and the convergence of the Rademacher exact series
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'besselI|besselJ|Bessel function' over both trees returns nothing: the only 'Bessel' occurrences are Bessel's inequality in inner-product spaces and Bessel potentials in the Sobolev files.

targets.target: Effective error terms and the distinction between truncated approximations and the infinite identity
targets.note: Nothing to make effective.

duplicates.note: ES.3 owns the circle-method major-arc machinery (singular integrals, local densities, convergence) that QM.2 names as its input; the Hardy-Ramanujan route is the partition instance of it.

targets.target: The weight-k hyperbolic Laplacian Delta_k
targets.note: Mathlib has harmonic functions on a complex/inner-product domain (the flat Laplacian) with the mean-value property, Liouville and the real-part-of-holomorphic characterization; there is no weight-k hyperbolic Laplacian on the upper half-plane and no Maass form (grep -rn -i 'maass' over both trees returns nothing).

targets.target: Growth conditions and the holomorphic/nonholomorphic Fourier parts of a harmonic weak Maass form
targets.note: No non-holomorphic modular objects exist in either library; Mathlib's ModularForm requires holomorphy.

targets.target: The xi operator and its kernel/image, with shadow weights
targets.note: No such operator is defined anywhere in either tree.

targets.target: Poincare series and the pairing/exact-sequence interface of Bruinier-Funke
targets.note: Mathlib has holomorphic Eisenstein series at level one and for congruence subgroups, which are the weight-zero Poincare series; general Poincare series and the Bruinier-Funke duality are absent.

targets.target: Indefinite theta functions in the sense of Zwegers
targets.note: Only the definite (positive-definite, rank-one) theta functions exist in Mathlib; there is no indefinite theta series and no error-function correction.

targets.target: Appell-Lerch sums
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'appell|lerch' over both trees returns nothing mathematical for this construction.

targets.target: Correction terms, transformation laws and shadows of mock modular forms
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'mock modular' over both trees returns nothing; no completion of a mock form exists.

targets.target: Source-scoped partition congruences
targets.note: Mathlib's only partition identity of this shape is Euler/Glaisher (an equality of counts, not a congruence); no Ramanujan-type congruence is proved in either library.

targets.target: Traces of singular moduli and special values
targets.note: There is no modular j-function in either library (grep -rn -i 'j-invariant|hauptmodul' over Mathlib/NumberTheory returns nothing), so singular moduli cannot be defined.

targets.target: Quantum modular forms and radial limits at roots of unity, compared with the unified WRT invariant
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'quantum modular|habiro|reshetikhin|colored jones' over both trees returns nothing; TauCeti has a knot-theory development but no quantum invariants of this kind.

targets.target: Eichler integrals, kept distinct from formal evaluations until an explicit comparison
targets.note: No Eichler integrals in either library.

duplicates.note: QT.7 owns the quantum-modularity statements and the example ledger linking cyclotomic coefficients, WRT values and Bloch regulators, which QM.5 imports and compares by radial limits.
HB.10 owns the explicit q-series/Nahm examples and boundaries that QM.5's radial-limit comparison draws on.

targets.target: Vertex-operator-algebra inputs and the moonshine module
targets.note: Mathlib defines a vertex operator as a Hahn-series-valued linear map with its coefficient API, but there is no vertex algebra or vertex operator algebra class (grep -rn 'VertexAlgebra' over Mathlib returns nothing), no no-ghost theorem and no moonshine module.

targets.target: The Monster group and its graded traces
targets.note: TauCeti records the Y_443 (Coxeter-plus-spider) presentation of M x 2 as a GroupPresentation with decidable transcription checks — a transcribed presentation, not a construction of the Monster and not a character table; there are no graded traces of any module.

targets.target: Modular transformation laws of the McKay-Thompson series and the genus-zero property
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'moonshine' over both trees returns nothing; there is no modular j-function, no hauptmodul and no genus-zero statement in either library.

targets.target: The Monster Lie algebra and the Borcherds denominator identity
targets.note: Mathlib has generalized Kac-Moody theory only through root systems and Lie algebra basics; no Borcherds-Kac-Moody algebra and no denominator identity exists.
